lead: Thyroid disease is common in pregnancy. Iodine needs rise, TBG doubles, and hCG stimulates the TSH receptor, so thyroid tests are read with free T4 and trimester ranges (TSH upper limit 2.5 in the first trimester, 3.0 later).
f: Graves' disease about 95% · Others: toxic nodular goitre, adenoma, thyroiditis, amiodarone, lithium · Graves': TRAb positive, goitre, eye signs; improves in late pregnancy, relapses after birth; needs antithyroid drugs · Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis: high hCG (hyperemesis, mole, twins), TRAb negative, no goitre or eye signs, settles by 18–20 wk: no antithyroid drugs

sc: Low TSH at 10 wk with exophthalmos → Graves': start PTU
Low TSH at 10 wk, vomiting, no goitre → Gestational: no drug

f: Weight loss despite appetite, tremor, resting pulse over 100, eye signs, goitre · TFTs: low TSH, high free T4; TRAb · Maternal: miscarriage, pre-eclampsia, heart failure, AF, thyroid storm · Fetal: preterm birth, FGR, stillbirth, fetal thyrotoxicosis, fetal goitre from drugs

tr: Past Graves' treated by surgery or radioiodine: still check TRAb; the antibodies cross the placenta (fetal heart over 160, goitre, FGR)

f: PTU 150–400 mg/day in the first trimester, then carbimazole 15–40 mg/day · Carbimazole embryopathy: aplasia cutis, choanal and oesophageal atresia · PTU: liver failure · Propranolol for a few weeks only (FGR) · Lowest dose keeping free T4 at the upper limit of normal; TFT every 4–6 wk · Breastfeeding safe at PTU under 150 or carbimazole under 15 mg/day

sc: On carbimazole, positive test at 6 wk → Switch to PTU
Graves' at 24 wk, well on PTU → Change to carbimazole

f: Poor control + trigger (labour, CS, infection) · Fever, confusion, tachycardia or AF, heart failure · HDU: fluids, cooling, propranolol, PTU, iodine 1 h after PTU, IV hydrocortisone; treat the trigger

sc: Fever, AF and confusion after CS → Thyroid storm

f: About 1%; Hashimoto's commonest; also thyroidectomy, radioiodine, iodine deficiency · High TSH, low free T4 · Risks: miscarriage, pre-eclampsia, low birth weight, stillbirth, lower IQ in the child · Raise levothyroxine by 25–30% as soon as pregnancy is confirmed · TSH each trimester and 6 wk after any change; target under 2.5 in the first trimester, under 3 later · Back to the pre-pregnancy dose after birth

sc: On thyroxine, TSH rising, takes it with ferrous sulphate → Take iron 4 h apart

f: Autoimmune; onset usually 3–4 months after birth · Hyper phase 1–4 months, hypo phase 4–8 months, most recover by 1 year · Hyper phase: beta-blocker, not antithyroid drugs · Hypo phase: thyroxine, stop at 6 months to test recovery · Recurs in 70%; yearly TFT

sc: Palpitations 3 months after birth, painless goitre → Thyroiditis: propranolol
